item.title: Spain's Council of Ministers is set to approve a 5.3% rise in the minimum wage to EUR 1,286 gross a month over 14 payments from 1 January 2027, above the 4.9% proposed by Labour Ministry experts, La Vanguardia reports.
item.description:
Spain's Council of Ministers is set to approve a 5.3% increase in the Interprofessional Minimum Wage, effective from 1 January 2027, La Vanguardia reports. The increase is EUR 65 a month, bringing the minimum wage to EUR 1,286 gross a month over fourteen payments. It is higher than the 4.9% proposed by experts from the Ministry of Labour; the ministry says the difference compensates for lost purchasing power, as the minimum wage rose 3.1% in 2026 against average inflation of 3.5%. The minimum wage remains exempt from income tax. MarketScreener reports, citing Labour Minister Yolanda Díaz, that the government intends to raise the minimum wage by 5.3% from next year, the ninth increase under the Socialist-led government since it came to power in 2018 and that the government says it should benefit more than 2.5 million workers. The rows do not give the cost to employers or the sectors with the most minimum-wage workers.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The rows describe a planned wage decision and the government's estimate of the workers affected, not its cost. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, a minimum wage rise above the 2026 average inflation rate raises labour costs most in labour-intensive sectors with many low-paid workers and supports household spending at the low end of the income scale. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, higher labour costs on building sites and in assembly can increase interest in products that shorten application time, while household income gains can support home improvement demand. Points that may be worth considering include the final approval, sector wage agreements and Spanish construction labour costs.

La Vanguardia | MarketScreener

item.title: Industrial production in the eurozone rose 0.2% in September, after a 0.5% fall in August, below the forecasts cited by Wallstreet:online and MarketScreener, which describes the figure as a preliminary estimate.
item.description:
Industrial production in the eurozone rose 0.2% in September, after falling 0.5% in August, Wallstreet:online and MarketScreener report; MarketScreener describes the figure as a preliminary estimate. Both outlets say the rise was below forecast but cite different figures: Wallstreet:online gives an economists' average of 0.3%, and MarketScreener a FXStreet forecast of 0.6%. The rows do not give a year-on-year change, a breakdown by country or by industry, or the source of the estimate.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The rows give one month's change in an aggregate index. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, a small rise after a larger fall leaves eurozone industrial output slightly lower over the two months, which does not point to a recovery in volumes. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, industrial adhesive demand in Europe follows manufacturing volumes in sectors such as vehicles, electronics, packaging and machinery, so the breakdown by industry decides where demand is moving. Points that may be worth considering include the country and sector breakdown, October data and the year-on-year trend.

Wallstreet:online | MarketScreener

item.title: Germany's automotive industry association VDA says planned tighter rules of origin for electric vehicle trade between the EU and Britain threaten a serious trade barrier, and asks for them to be postponed and raised at the 20 November EU–UK summit.
item.description:
The German Association of the Automotive Industry (VDA) says the planned tightening of rules of origin for trade in electric vehicles between the EU and Great Britain threatens to create a serious trade barrier, with competitive disadvantages for manufacturers on both sides. Instead of strengthening investment and value creation, it would add new burdens for companies. The VDA says the planned tightening, with impending tariffs, must be urgently postponed to avert damage to the automotive industry in Germany, Europe and the United Kingdom, and that the issue must be on the agenda of the EU–UK summit on 20 November. The row does not say when the tighter rules take effect, what local-content thresholds they set, what tariff rate would apply, or what the EU and UK governments plan.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The row is an industry association's position, not a government decision. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, rules of origin decide whether a vehicle crosses the border tariff-free, so stricter thresholds push carmakers to source batteries and components within the region or pay duty. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, battery and vehicle assembly use bonding and sealing materials, and a shift of battery and component sourcing changes where these materials are qualified and supplied in the EU and Britain. Points that may be worth considering include the summit outcome, the thresholds and dates in the rules, and any postponement.

VDA

item.title: The US Commerce Department issued an interim final rule on 16 November to stop third countries from remotely accessing advanced AI chips, which Reuters says may restrict China's access, Lianhe Zaobao reports.
item.description:
The US Commerce Department issued an interim final rule on 16 November to prevent third countries from remotely accessing advanced artificial intelligence chips, Lianhe Zaobao reports. The move aims to ensure that existing controls on sensitive US technology are not circumvented through remote computing arrangements in third-country data centres, and China's access to advanced AI chips may be restricted by the new rules, according to a Reuters report. The rule was issued as President Trump prepared for a trilateral meeting in Shenzhen with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. According to analysts quoted by Daily Sabah, the prospect of tighter US restrictions on China's access to advanced AI chips is likely to dominate discussions when Trump and Xi meet. The rows do not name the countries covered, the chip thresholds, the date the rule takes effect or a comment period.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The rows report a rule and its stated purpose, not its effect on trade. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, closing remote access through third countries narrows one route around chip export controls and can change where data-centre capacity for AI is built, and a rule issued days before a summit can become part of the negotiation. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, semiconductor packaging, electronics assembly and data-centre hardware use adhesives and thermal materials, so the location of AI computing capacity affects where this demand arises. Points that may be worth considering include the rule text, China's response and the outcome of the Shenzhen meeting.

Lianhe Zaobao | Daily Sabah

item.title: The US plastics industry accounted for more than USD 147 billion in global trade in 2025, ranking second in the Plastics Industry Association's global ranking, with domestic shipments up an estimated 1.2% to USD 358.4 billion.
item.description:
According to the Plastics Industry Association's (PLASTICS) 2026 Global Trends Report, the US plastics industry accounted for more than USD 147 billion in global trade in 2025. It ranked second in the association's 2025 Global Plastics Ranking, which is based on trade volume estimates across machinery, molds, materials and products. Domestic shipments increased by an estimated 1.2% to USD 358.4 billion, with exports accounting for 20.5% of shipments. Mexico and Canada remained the largest export destinations for US plastics, with exports of USD 19.2 billion and USD 13.5 billion respectively, and Mexico represented the industry's largest trade surplus at USD 10.8 billion, followed by Belgium and Brazil. The row does not name the country ranked first, does not split the USD 147 billion into exports and imports or by segment, does not say how much of the shipment growth reflects prices rather than volumes, and gives no figures for 2026.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The row gives annual trade and shipment values for 2025, not prices or 2026 data. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, a plastics industry whose two largest export markets are its neighbours depends on the terms of North American trade, and value-based shipment figures can rise with resin prices as well as with output. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, plastics are both a substrate that adhesives bond and a business that shares resin and additive supply chains with adhesive formulation, so the size and direction of plastics trade bear on raw-material flows and on bonding demand in plastic parts; the row gives no figures for adhesives. Points that may be worth considering include the split of the trade figure by segment, 2026 shipment data and US plastics exports to Mexico and Canada.

Plastics Industry Association

item.title: The average asking price of newly listed UK homes fell 1.8%, or GBP 6,745, from the previous month to GBP 364,270 in the four weeks to 7 November, which Rightmove attributes to higher mortgage rates linked to the US-Iran war.
item.description:
Figures released by the UK property website Rightmove show the average price of newly listed homes for sale in the UK at GBP 364,270 in the four weeks to 7 November, a decline of 1.8% or GBP 6,745 from the previous month, Commercial Times reports. Rightmove attributes the fall to a rise in mortgage rates as a result of the US-Iran war. The row does not give the year-on-year change, the number of new listings or completed sales, regional figures, or the level of mortgage rates.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The row gives one month's asking prices, the prices sellers set when they list a home, not the prices at which homes are sold or construction activity. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, falling asking prices with higher mortgage rates point to weaker buyer demand, which tends to reach housebuilding and home improvement with a delay. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, UK residential construction and renovation are users of flooring, tiling, sealing and insulation products, so a weaker housing market can lower demand in these segments if it continues. Points that may be worth considering include completed transaction data, housebuilding starts and the path of UK mortgage rates.

Commercial Times

item.title: Year-on-year falls in new-home prices in China's 70 large and medium-sized cities narrowed in October in first-, second- and third-tier cities, while month on month, second-tier prices fell 0.1% and third-tier 0.2%, NBS data show.
item.description:
According to National Bureau of Statistics data released on 16 November, reported by China Economic Net, sales prices of new commodity housing in first-tier cities were flat month on month in October, after a 0.1% rise in September. Second-tier prices fell 0.1%, after being flat in September, and third-tier prices fell 0.2%, the same rate as in September. For second-hand housing, first-tier prices rose 0.2% month on month, second-tier prices fell 0.3%, a decline 0.1 percentage points wider than in September, and third-tier prices fell 0.3%. Year on year, the decline in new-home prices narrowed by 0.4, 0.4 and 0.3 percentage points from September in first-, second- and third-tier cities, and the decline in second-hand prices by 1.1, 0.4 and 0.4 points. NBS spokesperson Fu Linghui said the market has seen certain positive changes with the adjustment of real estate policies, while some areas are still under pressure. Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development data show second-hand transactions by net signed area rose 11.4% year on year to 680 million square metres in the first ten months and has exceeded new-home sales area for several consecutive months. The rows do not give the level of the year-on-year declines, new-home sales volumes or construction starts.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The rows give price changes and second-hand transaction area, not new construction. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, narrowing price declines with month-on-month falls continuing outside the first tier describe a slower decline rather than a recovery, and a second-hand market larger than new-home sales by area shifts activity from new building towards renovation of existing homes. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, new residential construction and renovation draw on different products, from structural and installation adhesives to tile, floor and sealing products, so the balance between them matters as much as the price trend. Points that may be worth considering include new-home sales and construction starts, November price data and renovation activity.

China Economic Net | China Economic Net

item.title: China's carmakers' association issued a notice on 16 November under which 17 major automakers, including BYD, Geely and Chery, will be assessed on supplier payments, including whether small and medium-sized suppliers are paid within 60 days.
item.description:
The China Association of Automobile Manufacturers (CAAM) issued a notice on 16 November on the research and evaluation of automotive companies' payments to suppliers, Beijing Daily reports. Seventeen key automotive companies will be assessed on account periods and payment methods: whether they have payment management and digital systems, whether account periods for small and medium-sized suppliers do not exceed 60 days, the use of cash payments, and whether account periods for other suppliers comply with the 60-day requirement with cash and bank acceptance bill payments making up not less than 80%. The assessment agency will randomly select not less than 15 suppliers from each company to verify the information the companies submit, through information checks and on-site research. MarketScreener reports that CAAM and China's industry ministry announced the assessments will be annual, names BYD, Geely, Chery, Xiaomi and GAC among the companies, and reports the ministry as saying that carmakers with large overdue payables, deliberately extended payment cycles or frequent supplier complaints may be questioned and subject to corrective action; it describes the aim as a public scorecard on payment terms. The rows do not give the companies' current payment periods, when the first results will be published, or any penalty beyond corrective action.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The rows describe an assessment against stated payment benchmarks, not measured payment periods. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, an annual review with supplier verification and a possible public scorecard raises the cost to carmakers of stretching payment terms, and its effect depends on how strictly corrective action is applied and whether results are published by company. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, suppliers of bonding and sealing products to Chinese carmakers are among the creditors whose working capital depends on these terms, so shorter or more cash-based payment would reduce receivables, while carmakers under cost pressure may look for savings in prices instead. Points that may be worth considering include the publication of the first assessment, any named companies and later reported payables periods.

Beijing Daily | MarketScreener

item.title: Industry sales in Germany rose 4.6% year on year to EUR 546.3 billion in the third quarter, the highest in four years, while industrial employment fell 2.6% on the year to 5.3 million at end-September, an EY study shows, Süddeutsche Zeitung reports.
item.description:
According to a study by the consulting firm EY, reported by Süddeutsche Zeitung, industry sales in Germany increased 4.6% year on year to EUR 546.3 billion in the third quarter of 2026. It was the third consecutive quarterly increase and the highest figure in four years, and the report attributes it to the boom in artificial intelligence, price increases and billions in government spending on defence. Job cuts continue: 5.3 million people were employed in industry at the end of September, 140,200 or 2.6% fewer than a year earlier, and around 405,800 jobs, just over 7%, have been lost since the pre-pandemic year 2019. The row does not split sales by sector, does not give a price-adjusted figure, and does not say how much of the rise came from prices and how much from volumes.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The sales figure is nominal and the row names price increases among its causes, so it is not a measure of output. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, rising turnover with falling employment is consistent with growth concentrated in defence and AI-related segments and with price effects, rather than with a broad recovery in volumes. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, demand from German manufacturing customers follows production volumes more than sales values, so the split between price and volume, and between defence, electronics and other segments, is what decides how much of the rise reaches material consumption. Points that may be worth considering include EY's sector breakdown, price-adjusted production data and further industrial job figures.

Süddeutsche Zeitung

item.title: Global sales of new battery-electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles rose 8% year on year to 2.09 million in October and 5% to 17.5 million year to date, as China's year-on-year decline narrowed to 12%, Benchmark Mineral Intelligence reports.
item.description:
UK-based Benchmark Mineral Intelligence reported that global sales of new battery-electric and plug-in hybrid electric vehicles reached 2.09 million units in October, up 8% year on year, the Association of European Vehicle Logistics writes. Year-to-date volumes were up 5% to 17.5 million units. China's year-on-year decline narrowed to 12% as manufacturers continued to lean on exports, with passenger car new energy vehicle exports reaching almost 600,000 units, another monthly record. The row does not give October sales by region outside China, the split between battery-electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles, or the share of electric vehicles in total car sales.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The row gives unit sales, not values, and reports China's decline and record exports in the same month. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, global growth while China's home market shrinks means that growth sits outside China and that Chinese production is increasingly sold abroad, which moves where electric vehicles are bought and, over time, where they are assembled. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, electric vehicles use bonding, sealing and thermal management materials in battery packs and lightweight bodies, so where electric vehicle volumes grow affects where those materials are qualified and supplied. Points that may be worth considering include November sales data, regional splits and Chinese electric vehicle export volumes.

Association of European Vehicle Logistics
